title: Credit Controller
description:

title: IVA Administrator
description:
Corporate Insolvency Administrator

Location: Stockport

Salary: Competitive + Benefits

Imperium Financial Recruitment are acting as an agency on behalf of a well-established and highly regarded insolvency practice in Stockport, who are seeking to recruit a Corporate Insolvency Administrator to join their growing team.

This opportunity is suitable for either:
- An experienced Corporate Insolvency Administrator, or
- An IVA Administrator looking to transition into the corporate insolvency sector.

The successful candidate will work on a varied portfolio of corporate insolvency cases, with duties including closures and variations, alongside wider case administration responsibilities. The firm offers a supportive environment with genuine long-term progression opportunities.

For experienced candidates, the role can be office-based, hybrid, or fully remote.

Key Responsibilities:
- Managing corporate insolvency cases from inception through to closure
- Preparing closure documentation and handling case variations
- Liaising with directors, creditors, solicitors and other stakeholders
- Drafting reports and statutory documentation
- Supporting senior staff on a range of insolvency matters
- Ensuring all casework is compliant with current insolvency legislation and procedures

Requirements:
- Previous experience within corporate insolvency or IVA administration
- Strong organisational and communication skills
- Ability to manage workloads and meet deadlines effectively
- A professional and proactive approach to case management

This is an excellent opportunity to join a respected firm offering flexibility, stability, and career development within a successful insolvency team.

For further information or to apply confidentially, please contact Imperium Financial Recruitment.

title: Lettings Coordinator
description:
Property Coordinator

Stockport £28,000 + Quarterly Bonus (OTE £30,000)

Join a Business Building Something Big

This isn't your typical property role.

Our client is a fast-growing rental housing owner building a brand-new leasing and resident support function from the ground up. They're investing heavily, expanding across multiple regions and creating high-quality rental communities across both houses and apartments.

As a Property Coordinator, you'll play a key role in keeping everything running smoothly behind the scenes. You'll become the go-to person for prospects, residents and the wider leasing team, helping to deliver a seamless customer experience from first enquiry through to move-in.

This is a varied, fast-paced role where no two days are the same. Perfect for someone who loves organisation, enjoys helping people and takes pride in getting the details right.

What You'll Be Doing
- Coordinating enquiries, viewings and customer communications
- Supporting applicants through referencing and move-in processes
- Managing property listings, images, descriptions and online updates
- Keeping CRM records accurate and up to date
- Liaising with third-party providers and internal stakeholders
- Supporting residents with queries and general requests
- Monitoring applications and ensuring timelines are met
- Providing administrative and operational support to the wider leasing team

What We're Looking For
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Experience in coordination, administration, customer service or property is beneficial
- Comfortable managing multiple priorities at once
- Confident using systems, databases and CRM platforms
- A positive, proactive approach and willingness to learn
- Someone who enjoys being part of a growing business and making an impact

What's In It For You?
- £28,000 basic salary
- Quarterly bonus scheme (OTE £30,000)
- Genuine progression opportunities as the business grows
- Modern systems, technology and AI-supported processes
- Exposure to a rapidly expanding property platform
- A supportive, people-focused leadership team
- The chance to join at the beginning of an exciting growth journey

If you're looking for a role where you can be part of something ambitious, learn quickly and build a long-term career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: RTR Assistant Accountant
description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Record to Report Assistant Accountant to join a collaborative and supportive global finance team based in South Manchester This role is perfect for someone who thrives in an environment where accuracy, attention to detail, and continuous improvement are highly valued. As a key member of the record-to-report (R2 R) process team, you will play a vital part in ensuring that financial transactions are processed efficiently and in line with global standards. The organisation offers a welcoming atmosphere where your commitment to quality and your willingness to learn will be recognised and nurtured. With a competitive salary range of £32,000pa-£35,000pa,

As a Record to Report Assistant Accountant, you will immerse yourself in the heart of the organisation's global finance operations. Your daily responsibilities will revolve around executing transactional activities with precision while supporting critical month-end and year-end closing processes. You will be entrusted with upholding data integrity through diligent reconciliations and careful adherence to compliance requirements.

Specific duties include:
- Execute day-to-day transactional activities within the global record-to-report process, ensuring all tasks are completed accurately and efficiently according to established procedures.
- Support both month-end and year-end close activities by preparing reconciliations, processing journal entries, and maintaining data quality throughout the reporting cycle.
- Follow standard operating procedures (SOPs) and compliance requirements meticulously while escalating any exceptions or discrepancies to senior team members as needed.
- Maintain high standards of data integrity by regularly reviewing financial information for accuracy and completeness, contributing to reliable financial reporting.
- Collaborate closely with stakeholders across different functions and countries to improve service delivery and ensure alignment with global finance standards.
- Handle routine queries from internal teams or external partners promptly and professionally, providing clear explanations or directing more complex issues appropriately.
- Identify inefficiencies within existing processes by monitoring workflows and suggesting practical improvements that enhance overall efficiency.
- Support operational cycles by assisting with ad hoc tasks related to finance operations as required by the wider team or management.

The ideal candidate for the Record to Report Assistant Accountant position brings proven experience from similar roles within global finance environments where attention to detail was crucial. Your background includes exposure to record-to-report cycles, familiarity with ERP platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics F&O (or equivalent), and a solid grasp of fundamental accounting principles. You possess strong organisational capabilities which allow you to juggle competing demands without compromising on quality.

Ideally you will have experience in the following areas:
- Demonstrate experience of 1-3 years working within global record-to-report processes or similar finance roles where accuracy was paramount.
- A basic understanding of core finance processes including reconciliations, journal entries, and compliance requirements gained through previous employment or academic study.
- Familiarity with ERP systems is highly desirable; experience with Microsoft Dynamics F&O would be considered an advantage but is not essential.
- A relevant degree or professional qualification in accounting or finance is preferred though candidates qualified by experience will also be considered.
- Exceptional organisational skills that enable you to manage multiple priorities effectively while maintaining high standards of accuracy under tight deadlines.
- A process-driven mindset combined with a proactive attitude towards identifying areas for improvement within established workflows.
- Strong interpersonal skills that allow you to collaborate seamlessly with colleagues from diverse backgrounds both locally and internationally.
- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities enabling you to handle queries professionally and document work clearly for audit purposes.

This organisation stands out as a leader in its field thanks to its unwavering commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace where every team member feels valued. Employees benefit from flexible working arrangements designed around their needs alongside generous pension contributions that support long-term security.

If you are ready for your next step in finance within a supportive global team environment, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

Apply today by clicking on the link - take the first step towards joining a collaborative team where your contribution truly matters.

title: Import Coordinator
description:
Ocean Import Clerk

Location: Trafford Park, Manchester
Salary: Up to £30,000 per annum
Job Type: Permanent, Full Time

The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Ocean Import Clerk to join a well-established international freight forwarding business based in Trafford Park, Manchester.

Working within a busy ocean freight team, you will take responsibility for coordinating import shipments from origin through to final delivery, ensuring customers receive a professional, efficient and proactive service throughout.

This would suit someone with previous ocean imports or freight forwarding experience who is comfortable managing their own shipments and communicating with customers, shipping lines, overseas agents and suppliers.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing ocean import shipments from booking through to final delivery
- Handling both FCL and LCL import movements
- Liaising with shipping lines, overseas agents, hauliers and customers
- Tracking shipments and providing customers with regular updates
- Preparing and processing relevant import documentation
- Coordinating customs clearance requirements
- Arranging collections and onward deliveries
- Checking shipping documentation and ensuring information is accurate
- Managing vessel arrivals, releases and delivery instructions
- Monitoring potential delays, demurrage and storage issues
- Resolving shipment queries quickly and professionally
- Maintaining accurate records on internal freight systems
- Building strong relationships with customers and providing a high level of service

About You

We are looking for someone with:
- Previous experience within ocean/sea freight imports
- Experience gained within a freight forwarding or logistics environment
- Good understanding of the end-to-end import process
- Knowledge of FCL and LCL shipments
- Understanding of import and customs documentation
- Strong customer service and communication skills
- Good attention to detail and organisational ability
- Confidence managing multiple shipments and priorities simultaneously
- A proactive approach to problem solving
- Ability to work effectively as part of a busy freight forwarding team

What's on Offer?
- Salary up to £32,000
- Permanent position with an established international freight forwarding business
- Trafford Park location
- Opportunity to join an experienced and supportive team
- Exposure to international customers, suppliers and agents
- Genuine opportunity to develop your freight forwarding career

If you are interested in finding out more, please contact Adam Norris at Reed or apply now.

title: Team Administrator
description: Open to current NHS employee's only. Unfortunately this role does not attract sponsorship under current government legislation, therefore if you require a certificate of sponsorship to support a visa application, we will be unable to proceed with your application. An opportunity has arisen for a full time member of staff to join the NHS Talking Therapies Tameside & Glossop Administration Team. We are looking to employ a motivated and enthusiastic individual to join our fast paced Talking Therapies team from Monday to Friday. You will contribute to the general day to day running of the service by taking calls, covering reception, processing referrals and ensuring patients are seen in a timely manner in order to receive the best patient care possible. The Admin team is a high functioning, close working team which is reliant on team work and good communication skills. Previous experience of a busy office, multitasking, along with an ability to work under pressure, unsupervised and using your own initiative are essential. To provide efficient and effective administration support to the wider Talking Therapies Team in line with the Trust values of kindness, fairness, ingenuity and determination. Deal with enquiries from service uses, relatives, professionals and members of the public. Undertake the administration of all referrals received by the Service and provide administrative support to the clinicians within the team. To ensure high standards are maintained at all times and that work is produced effectively and efficiently in accordance with the Trust's policies and procedures. Accessing and inputting to clinical reporting systems - Pcmis. To undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. To undertake the comprehensive administration of all referrals received into the team. To ensure that all relevant referral information is recorded on PCMIS and other relevant information systems and be responsible for the security of the information contained within these systems. To collate all relevant available information to enable the effective triage of referrals received by the team. To take referrals and process from a range of multi-disciplinary professionals and agencies, service users and members of the public and provide practitioners with sufficient information in order to prioritise risk. To carry out general clerical duties including information gathering, dealing with internal and external post and photocopying documents. Deal with incoming postal and electronic mail as well as telephone enquiries and give advice wherever possible, using own initiative. To manage the appointments system for the team in line with clinic times and the off duty rota. To order and maintain sufficient levels of stationery and supplies for the team. To deal with telephone enquiries and give advice wherever possible, in a diplomatic and sensitive way, following these through with the appropriate member of staff, in a responsible and professional manner.

title: Administrator
description: Woodbank is a psychiatric intensive care unit for females aged 18 - 65. The unit provides support to women experiencing serious mental illness, such as psychosis and severe mood disorders. The post holder will be required to provide high quality administrative support to the unit, ensuring high standards are maintained at all times and work is produced effectively and efficiently. The post holder will be required to use independent judgement, sensitivity and discretion to carry out specified duties. Providing efficient general secretarial and administrative support to the Unit Manager, Clinical Services Manager, Occupational Therapists and Nursing team. To provide efficient general secretarial and administrative assistance to the Unit Manager, Clinical Services Manager, Occupational Therapist and their teams. Liaising with other members of staff on site, including maintenance and estates departments, GPs, patients and their relatives, and other relevant agencies, eg social services, probation, courts, prisons, police and solicitors. Collect, collate, input and extract data/info from NHS systems as directed by Unit Manager/Admin Manager (Paris, EASY, ESR). Order stock and non stock items for the unit. Input data onto Paris system with regards to admissions, discharges, AWOL, home leave, transfers and return to the ward. Responsible for the safe storage of data and information in accordance with Trust policies ensuring guidelines regarding confidentiality, disclosure of information and data protection are observed at all times. Maintain administrative systems set up to ensure an organised and efficient working environment for staff. To work as an integral part of the unit staff team. Developing and maintaining an efficient and effective filing system as required. Creation and formatting of documents including databases, daily paperwork, this includes regular housekeeping of documentation used on the unit. Dealing with telephone enquiries in a diplomatic and sensitive way, following these through with the relevant member of staff in an appropriate and tactful manner. Control and maintenance of health records in accordance with the Trust's record management policy and ensuring all are electronically tracked to the current location. To be responsible for the maintenance and security of a all manual and electronic filing systems. Co-operate fully in the introduction of new technology and new methods of working, as appropriate to the work of Unit Administrator, including self development, to continuously update knowledge of new trends. To safeguard, at all times, privacy of information relating to patients and staff alike, ensuring that an efficient, courteous service is offered to all service users and that confidentiality is strictly maintained. To work as an integral part of the RHS administration team as directed by the Admin Lead/Manager. To participate in the RHS Admin Forum. To participate in My Yearly Conversation reviews, undertaking management supervision and ensuring completion of mandatory training. To abide by all relevant Trust policies and procedures. Any other duties as required by the Trust.
